title: Torsors and etale $H^1$
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme and $M$ a finite abelian group. Then there is a
canonical bijection, natural in $(Y,M)$,

$$
\operatorname{Tor}^1(Y,M)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^1(Y_{\Et},\underline M)
$$

between the pointed set of isomorphism classes of $M$-torsors of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-torsors] and $H^1(Y_{\Et},\underline M)$, and an
$M$-torsor is the same thing as a finite etale surjective $Y$-scheme with an $M$-action simply
transitive on every geometric fibre. Moreover, let $Y$ be connected
with geometric point $\bar y$. For an $M$-torsor $P$, viewed as a finite
etale $Y$-scheme, and $p\in|P_{\bar y}|$, let
$f_P:\pi_1(Y,\bar y)\to M$ be defined by $g\cdot p=p+f_P(g)$; it is
a continuous homomorphism independent of $p$ and of $P$ within its
isomorphism class. Then $P$ is connected — that is, a Galois cover with
group $M$ — exactly when $f_P$ is surjective (the case of the sketch is
$M=\Z/d\Z$).
(Stacks 03AJ, 03RV, 0BND, together with the finite-etale correspondence; cf. Milne,
*Lectures on Etale Cohomology*, III.3.)

external.place: Milne, *Lectures on Etale Cohomology*, III.3.) The bijection, with its naturality, is [thm-galois-torsor-h1].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-torsor-h1] on the small etale site with $G=\underline M_Y$. This gives the canonical bijection $[T]\mapsto\delta_T(1)$. Every such $G$-torsor is finite locally constant by clause (2) of [lem-galois-etale-torsor-sheaf-torsor], so these are exactly the torsors of [def-weil-pbc-finite-torsors]; the trivial torsor maps to zero. No geometric point or connectedness is needed here. When a geometric point is chosen this is also the lifting-torsor bijection of [thm-galois-torsor-h1], whose statement supplies naturality in $(Y,M)$. Its construction realizes the first four paragraphs of the unit: a class represented by a quotient section is sent to its sheaf of lifts, and changing that section by a global lift gives translation of torsors. We use the general-site form above so that the first clause also covers the empty scheme.

For a scheme morphism $u:Y\to X$, [lem-sc-etale-torsor-inverse-image-extension] identifies the inverse image of $0\to G\to E_T\to\mathbf Z_X\to0$ with the canonical extension of $u^{-1}T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder], $u^*\delta_T(1)=\delta_{u^{-1}T}(u^*1)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-degree-zero], $u^*1$ is the pullback global section $1$. The canonical constant-sheaf comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-constant-sheaf] preserves every constant element; [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures] makes it the corresponding comparison of abelian sheaves. Thus, identifying $u^{-1}\underline M_X=\underline M_Y$, the equality is $u^*c_X(T)=c_Y(u^{-1}T)$. This proves scheme naturality without assuming either scheme connected.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, canonical extension and boundary construction; naturality proved here from the cited extension and cohomology statements

proof.text: For a homomorphism $\varphi:M\to N$ of finite abelian groups, apply [lem-sc-etale-torsor-pushout-extension] to the induced morphism of constant abelian sheaves. It gives a morphism of the canonical short exact sequences with endpoints $(\underline\varphi,\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf Z_Y})$ and identifies the target extension with that of the contracted-product $N$-torsor. The abelian-sheaf category has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Global sections are evaluation at the terminal object [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor]; kernels of abelian sheaves are computed sectionwise, so this functor is additive and left exact. Choose an ordinary injective resolution concentrated in nonnegative degrees. It is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], so it computes precisely the cohomology of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Thus we can compute that cohomology as the right-derived functors of global sections; [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] gives naturality of its boundary for a morphism of short exact sequences. Therefore $H^1(\underline\varphi)(\delta_T(1))=\delta_{T\wedge^M N}(1)$. Combining with step 2 proves naturality in both variables. The contracted-product torsor is finite locally constant by the same finite-constant torsor statement used in step 1.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, extension presentation; literature/stacks-project/derived.tex, Tags 015B and 05TE, boundary naturality

proof.text: Use [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-etale-equivalence], whose statement is for any scheme, to represent the finite locally constant underlying sheaf $T$ by a finite etale $Y$-scheme $P$, and to lift its $M$-action. Clause (3) of [lem-galois-etale-torsor-sheaf-torsor] gives the surjective scheme torsor and its torsor isomorphism $\coprod_{m\in M}P\cong P\times_Y P$. Conversely let $P$ be finite etale and surjective with the stated geometric-fibre action. Put $A=\coprod_{m\in M}P$, $B=P\times_Y P$, and let $a:A\to B$ send $(m,p)$ to $(m+p,p)$. Both are finite etale objects (finite coproducts and products under the cited equivalence). At every geometric point the map $a$ is bijective by simple transitivity. By [lem-galois-stalk-representable], these fibre maps are the maps on geometric stalks of $h_a$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-iso-on-geometric-stalks] makes $h_a$ an isomorphism, and full faithfulness of the finite-etale/sheaf equivalence makes $a$ an isomorphism. This verifies the scheme torsor condition, so clause (1) gives its sheaf torsor. The equivalence identifies equivariant isomorphisms, so this is an equivalence on isomorphism classes. Here simply transitive on geometric fibres includes nonemptiness; the surjectivity/local-section condition excludes the empty pseudo-torsor over a nonempty base. For the later pointed case [thm-galois-lc-etale] also identifies the fibre functors and explicitly preserves torsors and simply transitive actions.

Now assume $Y$ connected with geometric point $\bar y$. By [thm-galois-fundamental] the fibre $S=|P_{\bar y}|$ is a finite continuous $\pi_1$-set and each $M$-automorphism of $P$ is equivariant. By the torsor and fibre compatibility of [thm-galois-lc-etale], $S$ is a nonempty simply transitive $M$-set. Its $M$-action commutes with $\pi_1$ because $\pi_1$ consists of natural automorphisms of the fibre functor [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Choose $p\in S$. The bijection $M\to S$, $a\mapsto p+a$, uniquely defines $f_P(g)$ by $gp=p+f_P(g)$.

Commutation gives $ghp=g(p+f_P(h))=p+f_P(g)+f_P(h)$, hence $f_P(gh)=f_P(g)+f_P(h)$ by uniqueness; also $f_P(1)=0$. For each $m\in M$, the inverse image $f_P^{-1}(m)=\{g:gp=p+m\}$ is open by continuity of the action on the discrete finite set $S$, as specified in [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Since $M$ is discrete this proves continuity. If $p_1=p+a$, then $gp_1=p+f_P(g)+a=p_1+f_P(g)$, using abelianity; thus the character is independent of $p$. An equivariant torsor isomorphism sends $gp=p+f_P(g)$ to the identical equation in the other fibre, so the character is independent of the representative.

source.place: Tag 0BND and blueprint sbc-prop-torsors-h1, paragraph The homomorphism; explicit elementary calculation

proof.text: If $P$ is connected as a scheme, [lem-galois-finite-etale-connected-object] makes it a connected object of $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$. Under [thm-galois-fundamental], monomorphisms correspond to inclusions of invariant subsets and the initial object to the empty set. By [def-galois-connected-object], the nonempty set $S$ has no proper nonempty invariant subset; each orbit is such a subset, so $S$ is transitive. Conversely, suppose $S$ transitive. Let $V$ be any clopen subset of $P$. By [lem-galois-coproduct-copies-morphisms-clopen] with $U=Y$, $E=\{0,1\}$ and $W=P$, the partition $(V,P\setminus V)$ defines a $Y$-morphism $P\to Y\amalg Y$. The equivalence [thm-galois-fundamental] preserves this coproduct and its coprojections; the fibre of $Y$ is a singleton, so the target is the trivial two-point $\pi_1$-set. An equivariant map from a transitive set to it is constant. Faithfulness makes the original morphism one of the two constant coprojection maps. Clause (c) of the clopen-decomposition statement then forces $V=\varnothing$ or $V=P$. Also $P$ is nonempty because its fibre $S$ is. This is exactly topological connectedness of $P$. Finally the orbit of $p$ is $p+f_P(\pi_1)$ and $a\mapsto p+a$ is a bijection $M\to S$, so transitivity is equivalent to surjectivity of $f_P$.

If $P$ is connected, [lem-fet-galois-category] supplies the Galois category to which [lem-galois-axioms] applies. The translations define an injective homomorphism $M\to\operatorname{Aut}_Y(P)$: a translation which is the identity fixes $p$, and simple transitivity forces its element to be zero. Since $|S|=|M|$, clause (6) of [lem-galois-axioms] bounds $|\operatorname{Aut}_Y(P)|$ by $|S|=|M|$. Thus the injection is onto, identifies $M$ with the entire automorphism group, and this group acts simply transitively on $S$. Together with connectedness this is a Galois cover by [def-galois-object]. Conversely that definition includes connectedness. This proves the final parenthetical equivalence with no assumption that $M$ is cyclic.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme and $M$ a finite abelian group. Then there is a
canonical bijection, natural in $(Y,M)$,

$$
\operatorname{Tor}^1(Y,M)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^1(Y_{\Et},\underline M)
$$

between the pointed set of isomorphism classes of $M$-torsors of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-torsors] and $H^1(Y_{\Et},\underline M)$, and an
$M$-torsor is the same thing as a finite etale $Y$-scheme, surjective over
$Y$, with a simply transitive $M$-action. Moreover, let $Y$ be connected
with geometric point $\bar y$. For an $M$-torsor $P$, viewed as a finite
etale $Y$-scheme, and $p\in|P_{\bar y}|$, let
$f_P:\pi_1(Y,\bar y)\to M$ be defined by $g\cdot p=p+f_P(g)$; it is
a continuous homomorphism independent of $p$ and of $P$ within its
isomorphism class. Then $P$ is connected — that is, a Galois cover with
group $M$ — exactly when $f_P$ is surjective.

proof.text:
The bijection, with its naturality, is [thm-galois-torsor-h1]. By
[thm-galois-lc-etale] the functor
$P\mapsto\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_Y(-,P)$ is an equivalence from
finite etale $Y$-schemes to finite locally constant sheaves which carries
simply transitive $M$-actions to simply transitive ones, and conversely;
since an $M$-torsor is by [def-weil-pbc-finite-torsors] a sheaf with an
$M$-action for which $M\times P\to P\times_YP$ is an isomorphism and which
has sections locally, $M$-torsors are the same as finite etale $Y$-schemes,
surjective over $Y$, with a simply transitive $M$-action.

Now let $Y$ be connected and $P$ an $M$-torsor, viewed as a
finite etale $Y$-scheme with $M$ acting by $Y$-automorphisms. By
[thm-galois-fundamental] the fibre functor $F_{\bar y}$ of
[def-galois-fibre-functor] identifies $P$ with the finite continuous
$\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$-set $|P_{\bar y}|$, and the $M$-action with an action
of $M$ on $|P_{\bar y}|$ by $\pi_1$-equivariant maps; this action is
simply transitive because the isomorphism $M\times P\to P\times_YP$
becomes $M\times|P_{\bar y}|\cong|P_{\bar y}|\times|P_{\bar y}|$ under
the exact functor $F_{\bar y}$, and $|P_{\bar y}|\neq\emptyset$ because
$P\to Y$ is surjective.

*The homomorphism.* Fix $p\in|P_{\bar y}|$. By simple transitivity there
is a unique $f_P(g)\in M$ with $g\cdot p=p+f_P(g)$. As the two actions
commute,
$gh\cdot p=g\cdot(p+f_P(h))=(g\cdot p)+f_P(h)=p+f_P(g)+f_P(h)$, so
$f_P$ is a homomorphism. It is continuous: for $m\in M$ the set
$\{g:f_P(g)=m\}$ is the stabilizer-coset $\{g:g\cdot p=p+m\}$, which
is open because the action on the finite discrete set $|P_{\bar y}|$ is
continuous (the definition of a $\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$-set in
[def-galois-fibre-functor]). Replacing $p$ by $p+a$ gives
$g\cdot(p+a)=p+a+f_P(g)$, so $f_P$ does not depend on $p$, $M$ being
abelian; and an $M$-equivariant isomorphism $P\cong P'$ carries $p$ to a
point $p'$ with the same $f$, so $f_P$ only depends on the class of $P$,
hence (by the bijection) on the class in $H^1(Y_{\Et},\underline M)$.

*Connectedness.* By [lem-fet-galois-category], $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$
with $F_{\bar y}$ is a Galois category whose connected objects are the
connected finite etale $Y$-schemes, and the equivalence of
[thm-galois-fundamental] preserves finite coproducts and initial
objects, so $P$ is connected exactly when the nonempty
$\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$-set $|P_{\bar y}|$ is not a disjoint union of two
nonempty sub-$\pi_1$-sets, i.e. exactly when $\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$ acts
transitively on it (each orbit is a sub-$\pi_1$-set with an invariant
complement). Since $p\mapsto p+m$ is a bijection $M\to|P_{\bar y}|$
and the orbit of $p$ is $p+f_P(\pi_1(Y,\bar y))$, the action is
transitive exactly when $f_P$ is surjective.

*Galois.* If $P$ is connected, $M$ acts on $P$ by
$Y$-automorphisms, faithfully and transitively on the fibre
$|P_{\bar y}|$ of cardinality $\#M$, so $\#\operatorname{Aut}(P)\ge\#M$;
by [lem-galois-axioms] (6) $\#\operatorname{Aut}(P)\le\#|P_{\bar y}|=\#M$.
Hence $\operatorname{Aut}(P)=M$ acts simply transitively on the
fibre, and $P$ is a Galois cover with group $M$. Conversely a
Galois cover is connected by definition.
